plan: Given my value of $6, I should aim to bid just below this to ensure a positive profit if I win. Bidding too high risks winning and paying more than my value, resulting in a loss. Since there's no history to consider, I will bid $5.9. This bid maximizes the chance of winning while keeping the worst-case scenario (paying $0 if others bid higher) acceptable.

Given my value of $40, I aim to bid below this to ensure a profit if I win. To maximize profit, I should bid slightly above the average expected value of the other bidders, around $24.5. This balances winning chances while minimizing cost. Worst-case, if others bid higher, I lose nothing. If I win, I pay the third-highest bid, ideally much lower than my valuation, securing profit. I choose to bid $25, as it’s competitive but leaves room for profit if I win.

Considering my value of $28, I aim to bid just below my value to maximize profit while minimizing risk. Bidding slightly lower accounts for the worst-case scenario where I might overpay if others bid high. A bid of $27.9 ensures I still make a profit if I win and pay a third-highest bid close to the others'. This bid is competitive yet conservative, balancing potential gain and loss.
